items.text: REFERRED TO HOUSING, CONSTRUCTION AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT

items.lawCode: Amd §47, Priv Hous Fin L; amd §6, Chap 514 of 1983; amd §7, Chap 396 of 1984
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3458

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the private housing finance law, in
relation to an increase in bond and note authorization of the New York
state housing finance agency; and to amend chapter 514 of the laws of
1983, amending the private housing finance law and the real property
tax law relating to the powers of the New York state housing finance
agency to finance certain multi-family housing; and to amend chapter
396 of the laws of 1984, amending the private housing finance law and
the real property tax law relating to the powers of the New York state
housing finance agency to finance certain multi-family housing, in
relation to the effectiveness of such chapters

 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :  This bill would (i) increase by $1 billion the
maximum bonding authority of the New York State Housing Finance Agency
("HFA") from $13.78 billion to $14.78 billion and (ii) extend HFA's
authority to issue bonds to June 30, 2011.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :  Section 1 of the bill would increase the
bonding authority of HFA to a maximum of $14.78 billion.

Sections 2 and 3 of the bill would extend HFA's authority to finance
certain multi-family housing projects until June 30, 2011.

Section 4 of the bill provides for an immediate effective date.

 EXISTING LAW :  Current law authorizes HFA to issue bonds and notes
for its housing programs for any of its corporate purposes in an
aggregate principal amount not to exceed $13.78 billion.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :  Since 2000, similar bills have been
enacted on an annual basis to increase HFA's bonding authority and on
a biennial basis to extend HFA's authority to issue bonds. See Chapter
152 of the Laws of 2009: Chapter 85 of the Laws of 2007; Chapter 398
of the Laws of 2006: Chapter 124 of the Laws of 2005: Chapter 204 of
the Laws of 2004: Chapter 99 of the Laws of 2003; Chapter 48 of the
Laws of 2002: Chapter 363 of the Laws of 2001; and Chapter 131 of the
Laws of 2000.

 STATEMENT IN SUPPORT :  This bill would increase the maximum amount
of new money bonds which HFA is authorized to issue and would extend
HFA's authority to finance certain multi-family housing projects until
June 30. 2011.  HFA currently has a substantial pipeline of financing
requests that will result in both the creation and preservation of
affordable housing across New York State. The bill would increase
HFA's authority to issue bonds up to a total maximum amount of $14.78
billion, which will enable HFA to continue to meet the housing demands
of New Yorkers, as well as creating jobs and providing economic
stimulus.

 BUDGET IMPLICATIONS :  None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :  This bill takes effect immediately.

BILL NUMBER:  S3458A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the private housing finance law, in relation to an
increase in bond and note authorization of the New York state housing

 PURPOSE :

This bill would (i) increase by $500 million the maximum bonding
authority of the New York State Housing Finance Agency ("HFA") from
$13.78 billion to $14.28 billion and (ii) extend HFA's authority to
issue bonds to June 30, 2011.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill would increase the bonding authority of HFA to a
maximum of $14.28 billion. Sections 2 and 3 of the bill would extend
HFA's authority to finance certain multi-family housing projects until
June 30, 2011. Section 4 of the bill provides for an immediate
effective date.

 EXISTING LAW :

Current law authorizes HFA to issue bonds and notes for its housing
programs for any of its corporate purposes in an aggregate principal
amount not to exceed $13.78 billion.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This bill would increase the maximum amount of new money bonds which
HFA is authorized to issue and would extend HFA's authority to finance
certain multi-family housing projects until June 30, 2011.  HFA
currently has a substantial pipeline of financing requests that will
result in both the creation and preservation of affordable housing
across New York State. The bill would increase HFA's authority to
issue bonds up to a total maximum amount of $14.28 billion, which will
enable HFA to continue to meet the housing demands of New Yorkers, as
well as creating jobs and providing economic stimulus.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

Since 2000, similar bills have been enacted on an annual basis to
increase HFA's bonding authority and on a biennial basis to extend
HFA's authority to issue bonds. See Chapter 152 of the Laws of 2009:
Chapter 85 of the Laws of 2007; Chapter 398 of the Laws of 2006:
Chapter 124 of the Laws of 2005: Chapter 204 of the Laws of 2004:
Chapter 99 of the Laws of 2003; Chapter 48 of the Laws of 2002:
Chapter 363 of the Laws of 2001; and Chapter 131 of the Laws of 2000.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This bill takes effect immediately.
